info.title: Salsa Engage Integration API
info.description:
## General Description
This API is useful for integrating Salsa Engage data into other CRM systems. Engage API allows you to push supporters, groups, and transactions to another system, and pull all those things plus activity data from that system. You'll need an application in the middle to transfer the data back and forth and transform it so that each system understands it. Engage uses JSON for transferring data. Fields that have no value (NULL in our database) will NOT be included in results. You may specify nulls explicitly in your request if you desire. 

Base URL for all calls: https://api.salsalabs.org/api

# Authentication

<!-- ReDoc-Inject: <security-definitions> -->

tags.name: Call Rate Limits
tags.description:
Salsa Engage doesn't limit the number of concurrent processes that can access the API, but it does impose the following call rate limit:

Your token will allow: 
* Up to 300 calls to the API within a 1 minute period
* Up to 20 items included in batch/bulk calls - this includes multiple supporter updates as well as searching and pagination calls

Each item in a batch counts as 1 call and will be counted for the 1 minute period.
For example 15 calls with a batch of 20  equates to 300 calls and will cause rate limiting to be enforced.
Rate limiting is performed with a rolling 1 minute window - this means you can not perform 300 operations at the end of one clock minute and immediately send 300 more calls when the next clock minute occurs.
**If your organization requires a higher call rate limit, you can speak to a sales representative to discuss increasing it.**

tags.name: HTML Error Codes
tags.description: | HTTP Code | Name | Description | |:-----------:|:-----------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | 400 | Bad Request | **Directives in your payload were invalid** This error would typically occur if the parameters for a search operation are not configured correctly. Such an example is a activity search request without the *modifiedFrom* attribute set within the payload. In addition to the 400 code, the system will include a description for what the problem was. For example 400 Bad Request - Either 'modifiedFrom' or 'activityIds' must be provided. | | 401 | Unauthorized | Returned when a request with an invalid or missing token is made | | 405 | Method Not Allowed | Returned when a request is made to modify an object that is not allowed to be changed via the API, for example, trying to change a static segment. | | 429 | Too Many Requests | A 429 error code will be returned in one of two cases. Either the call rate for the token has been exceeded, or the batch size requested for an operation is larger than what is configured for your token.In either case the 429 will be returned with either one of the following messages: *429 Call rate has been exceeded* or *429 Requested batch size exceeds the allowed size of: \* | | 500 | Internal Server Error | This exception will also include a JSON structure in the body with additional contextual information which could be provided to Salsa for troubleshooting. You should be aware that some of these errors reported in this manner can be resolved on your end. An example of,such an error is providing an incorrect date format for a search condition |

tags.name: Pagination
tags.description: Many of the API calls support the use of **count** and **offset** options to enable pagination of results.  An **offset** value will be used to index the results out of the total possible.  So if you request a **count** of 20, with **offset** you will receive the first 20 results.  Specifying an offset of **20** will then return you the next batch of 20 results, etc.

tags.name: Country/State
tags.description: Salsa Engage uses ISO standards to validate countries and state/provinces within a country. In general, specify countries via their **ISO 3166-1 alpha 2** code. Similarly, specify states/provinces via their **ISO 3166-2** code, which normally consists of the 2 character country code followed by \'-\' and the 2 or 3 character state/province code. For the US, specify just the 2 character state code directly, without the \'US-\' prefix. For more information, please visit ISO-3166-1 alpha 2 and ISO-3166-2

tags.name: General Calls
tags.description: This API endpoint enables you to programmatically understand how many calls are available before making a request. The returned payload will include the count of available calls as well as operations that have been performed to date for the token.

tags.name: Email Results
tags.description: These API endpoints provide the ability to retrieve email activity data so that integrations or third-parties can use that data for segmentation/scoring externally. For instance, when invoked, Salesforce customers have a way to pull back data without necessarily storing it in Salesforce and creating storage concerns.

tags.name: Merge Supporter Records
tags.description: This API endpoint provides the ability to fully merge all activity data for two supporter records. When invoked, all activities performed by one supporter will be merged into another supporter and the supporter whose records were merged will be deleted from the system. This call enables the ability to consolidate two supporter records into a single supporter record. Please be aware that this call will primarily merge the activity records and not census data—that is the responsibility of the caller. **WARNING: It should also be understood that this operation is NOT reversible.**

tags.name: Supporter Data
tags.description: These API endpoints allow you to fully manage the census information about a supporter.

tags.name: Transaction
tags.description: These API endpoints allow you to search the information about donation intent and donation transaction data.

tags.name: Activity Data
tags.description:
Activities represent the interaction of supporters with published forms.  At this time, supporters can interact with the following types of forms:

* *SUBSCRIPTION_MANAGEMENT* -- Make changes to email interests as well as globally opting out
* *SUBSCRIBE* -- Signup to become a supporter of your organization
* *FUNDRAISE* -- Make a donation to your organization
* *PETITION* -- Sign a petition to show their support for your organization's cause
* *TARGETED_LETTER* -- Send a letter to political leaders within their district
* *TICKETED_EVENT* -- Attend an event, or donate to the cause of an event
* *P2P_EVENT* -- Participated in a Peer 2 Peer Event, or donated to one
* *FACEBOOK_AD* -- Submitted an ad on Facebook
* *REGULATION_COMMENTS* -- Submitted a regulations.gov comment

tags.name: Segment Data
tags.description: This API endpoint allows you to retrieve information about segments. Segments provide the ability for you to logically group supporters and then use the grouping to target supporters in an email blast or export.

tags.name: Offline Donations
tags.description:
These API endpoints enable add and update functionality for offline donations. Offline donations can be classified as those donations that were captured/processed by a system other than the Salsa Online/CRM system. These donations can be added to include them in the Online dashboard, reports, and segmentation functionality as well as the equivalent functionality in CRM system.

**Note: Donations added via the API cannot be deleted. This is due to the number of places where this data is propagated. They can only be zeroed out or refunded.**

tags.name: Email Blast
tags.description: These API endpoints allow you to create an email blast, assign targets and schedule or send the blast.

tags.name: Activity Forms
tags.description:
These API endpoints enable the creation, update and publication control of forms. Note, for form field attributes, leaving out a value indicates that either the default value applies, or no change to any existing values will be made. Any exceptions will be noted in the documentation of the attribute. Also note that each type of form has a minimum set of required fields that **must** be defined on the form before it can be published. Those fields will be marked as ***hardRequired***.
Display of form elements is based on a 12-column grid. This API allows you to control the width of each field by specifying how many columns it will take up (out of the available 12 for a row). See [Grid](https://get.foundation/sites/docs-v5/components/grid.html "Foundation 5 Grid") for more details.

tags.name: AutoResponder
tags.description: These API endpoints allow you to manage the autoresponders for specific forms.

tags.name: Custom Fields
tags.description: These API endpoints allow you to retrieve, create, and update both supporter and activity custom fields

post.description:
Searching for supporters can be performed as follows:

* Specifying a list of ids such as email address, external id, or Salsa Engage id. It should be understood that the provided ids must all be of the same type - passing a mix of ids is not supported.
* Specifying a *modifiedFrom* date and optional a *modifiedTo* date to search for those who were modified on or after or in between that criteria - note that this is for modification of their census data(First Name, Last Name, Address, Contacts, etc)
* Specifying a *searchString* that will search first name, last, email and/or cell phone

### Fundraise

Depending on the flag you configure on the form, you can use either a single auto responder for all donations, or specific ones based on interval

* **DonationSuccess** - This message will be sent to your supporters each time a donation payment is successful.

***OR*** 

* **DonationSuccessOneTime** - This message will be sent for a successful one time donation.

* **DonationSuccessMonthlyInitial** -- This message will be sent for the initial monthly recurring donation.

* **DonationSuccessMonthlyInstallment** -- This message will be sent for any subsequent recurring monthly donations.

* **DonationSuccessQuarterlyInitial** -- This message will be sent for the initial quarterly recurring donation.

* **DonationSuccessQuarterlyInstallment** -- This message will be sent for any subsequent recurring quarterly donations.

* **DonationSuccessAnnualInitial** -- This message will be sent for the initial annual recurring donation.

* **DonationSuccessAnnualInstallment** -- This message will be sent for any subsequent annual recurring donations.

### Subscribe

* **SignUpFormSubmit** - This is the default message for sign-up forms. Supporters will receive this email when they sign up for your email list.

### Petition

* **PetitionSubmit** - This is the default message for petition signers. Supporters will receive this email when they sign one of your petitions.

### TargetedLetter

* **TargetedLetterSubmit** - This is the default message for targeted letters. Supporters will receive this email when they send a targeted letter.

* **TargetedLetterOutOfDistrict** - Targeted Action Ineligible Follow Up

### RegulationComment

* **RegulationCommentsSubmit** - This is the default message for regulation document signers. Supporters will receive this email when they sign one of your regulation documents.

### TicketedEvent

* **TicketedEventSubmit** - This is a default message for Events and Events + Donations. Supporters will receive this email after they register for an event or register and donate.

id.description: optional client supplied ID for a request, that will be returned in any response

id.description: engage generated UUID for the custom field. Should not be included for new custom fields; it is required for updates

type.description: the type of custom field; required for new custom fields, will be ignored for updates

activityType.description: if the type is Supporter, this will be blank; if the type is Activity, this is required for new custom fields. this will be ignored for updates

fieldName.description: the name of the custom field, must be unique

fieldType.description: what sort of html input control should be rendered for the answer; required for new custom fields, will be ignored for updates

dataType.description:
what kind of answer to expect; required for new custom fields, will be ignored for updates

"Boolean" values will always have a fieldType of "Radio"

and must always have answerOptions of True/False or Yes/No



"Number" and "BigDecimal" values must always have a fieldType of "Input"

description.description:
the description of the custom field

When updating, this field is ignored if it is not included.

If you wish to clear this, you must send "#N/A" as the value.

createdDate.description: date that the field was first created

modifiedDate.description: the most recent time the field has been updated

answerOptions.description:
the possible options for Select and Radio fieldType lists.

When updating, answerOptions cannot be removed, only hidden (in case someone has selected the option).

To hide an answerOption, remove it from the answerOptions field, and add it to the hiddenAnswerOptions field.

items.description:
the possible options for Select and Radio fieldType lists.

When updating, answerOptions cannot be removed, only hidden (in case someone has selected the option).

To hide an answerOption, remove it from the answerOptions field, and add it to the hiddenAnswerOptions field.

hiddenAnswerOptions.description: options for Select fieldType lists that have been hidden/are no longer valid

items.description: options for Select fieldType lists that have been hidden/are no longer valid

validationParams.description: rules for validating the values for the custom fields

placeholderText.description:
helper text displayed in the input control, only used for fieldType "Input"

When updating, this field is ignored if it is not included.

If you wish to clear this, you must send "#N/A" as the value.

parameterName.description: unique name used to identify the input in the html, limited to letters, numbers, and underscores; required for new custom fields, ignored for updates

CustomField.description: this object contains information about a custom field.

count.description: the count of elements in the **results** list

CustomFields.description: this object contains a list of custom fields

count.description: the count of elements in the **results** list

PayloadCustomFields.description: contents of the response or request, expand for details

validationKey.description:
name of the validation parameter.

When updating, if a validation key is not sent, it will not be changed.

Acceptable values are:

"Default Value": Required for Select and Radio Inputs

"Text Restriction": Valid for Input fieldTypes. Limits the character types the form control should accept.

"Maximum Date": Valid for Date dataTypes

"Minimum Date": Valid for Date dataTypes

"Maximum Time": Valid for Date dataTypes

"Minimum Time": Valid for Date dataTypes

"Maximum Size": Valid for Input and TextArea fieldTypes

"Minimum Size": Valid for Input and TextArea fieldTypes

validationValue.description:
the value of the validation parameter.

This is always submitted as a String.
Acceptable values depend on the validationKey:"Default Value": Should be one of the values included in answerOptions

"Text Restriction": Must be one of AnyCharacter, AlphaOnly, NumericOnly, AlphaNumeric

"Maximum Date": Date value using "yyyy-MM-dd" format

"Minimum Date": Date value using "yyyy-MM-dd" format

"Maximum Time": Time value using "HH:mm:ss" format

"Minimum Time": Time value using "HH:mm:ss" format

"Maximum Size": Number, maximum value of 256 for Input fieldType, 2000 for TextArea fieldType

"Minimum Size": Number, minimum value of 0
